business_scope.primary_industry_name: Interactive Language Education and Automated Tutoring Software

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Agreement between the Belgo-Luxembourg Economic Union (BLEU) and the People's Republic of China for the Promotion and Protection of Investments (signed 2005, in force 2009)
Convention between the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg and the People's Republic of China for the Avoidance of Double Taxation with respect to Taxes on Income and Capital (signed 1994, in force 1995)
Convention between the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg and the United States of America for the Avoidance of Double Taxation (signed 1996, in force 2000)
EU-Canada Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA, provisionally applied from 21 September 2017)
Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union - Articles 49 to 54 (freedom of establishment, directly applicable in Luxembourg)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: AML/CFT and UBO framework: (i) Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended; (ii) Law of 10 August 2018 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing; (iii) Law of 25 March 2020 transposing Directive (EU) 2018/843 (5AMLD); (iv) Law of 13 January 2019 instituting the Register of Beneficial Owners (Registre des Beneficiaires Effectifs - RBE), as amended; (v) CSSF Regulation No. 12-02 of 14 December 2012, as amended; and (vi) CSSF Circular 18/698 on anti-bribery and corruption. Supervisory authorities: Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for regulated obliged entities, the Luxembourg Business Registers unit for RBE filings, and the Public Prosecutor's Office for criminal enforcement.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of valid passport or national identity card (each shareholder, beneficial owner and proposed manager)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National civil registry or licensed notary of the individual's country of origin; original passport must be produced for verification before the Luxembourg notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; for PRC-origin documents the apostille regime applies as of 7 November 2023 (China accession to the 1961 Hague Convention); sworn French translation required where the document is not in French, English, German or Luxembourgish

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (utility bill, bank statement or official municipal residence certificate) dated within three months
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility company, credit institution, or municipal registry of the individual's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization where the issuing state is not party to the 1961 Hague Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Criminal record extract / police clearance certificate (for each proposed manager and authorised signatory)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National criminal records authority (e.g., Casier Judiciaire) of the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization; sworn French translation required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / excerpt from the commercial register (for any corporate shareholder)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official companies registry of the corporate shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization; French translation required for RCS filing

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter or evidence of initial capital deposit (blocked account certificate issued by the receiving credit institution)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Credit institution in Luxembourg or another EU/EEA member state holding the paid-up capital subscription funds
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Banking-channel confirmation accepted; no apostille required, but the Luxembourg notary must receive direct written confirmation of the deposit before signing the deed

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based due diligence at formation by the appointed notary, fiduciary and bank covers: (i) PEP status under the revised FATF Recommendations 12 and 24; (ii) UN Security Council consolidated sanctions lists; (iii) EU Council financial sanctions regulations and Luxembourg implementing measures, including asset-freezing regimes; (iv) OFAC SDN and Consolidated Sanctions List where USD clearing or US-market counterparties are contemplated; (v) national insolvency and disqualification registers; and (vi) adverse media and financial-crime databases. Every UBO above the 25% threshold must be CDD-verified in full. PEP relationships trigger enhanced due diligence, including documented source of wealth and source of funds; rescreening is mandatory at any change of shareholding, at each anniversary, and upon any triggering event such as a major subscription, new payment rail or new-market deployment.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Societes (RCS) portal at https://www.lbr.lu; name search, reservation and electronic filing are effected through the MyLBR professional e-filing interface
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be written in Latin-script characters. A non-Latin operative name may be registered only in a strictly transliterated form that is unambiguous and searchable in the RCS index. The name must be distinctive, not misleading, and must not conflict with names or marks already registered in the RCS. The legal-form suffix must appear as 'SARL' or as the full French denomination 'Societe a Responsabilite Limitee'; the operative part may be in English or any other Latin-script language, but French is preferred for administrative consistency and to avoid rejection.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque, Bank, Banking (requires CSSF authorisation and prior Ministry of Finance clearance)
Fiduciaire, Fiduciary, Trustee (requires licensing under fiduciary-services legislation)
Fonds, Fund, SICAV, SIF, RAIF (investment-fund terminology requiring CSSF/ALFI substance vetting)
Bourse, Stock Exchange, Trading Platform (regulated financial market terminology)
Chambre de Commerce, Chamber of Commerce (institutional designation protected by statute)
Luxembourg, Luxemburg, Letzebuerg (when implying state patronage or official connection)
Etat, State, Commune, Municipal, Universite, Academie, Ecole (public or educational accreditation terms requiring ministerial approval; relevant to EdTech naming)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon RCS name rejection: (1) the applicant may request a written statement of reasons from the RCS; (2) an amended name may be re-filed immediately via the MyLBR portal, with an additional reservation fee; (3) a formal appeal (recours) against the refusal may be lodged with the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg, commercial chamber, within one month of notification, pursuant to Article 18 of the Law of 19 December 2002; (4) concurrently, an administrative reconsideration request (reclamation gracieuse) may be addressed to the RCS registrar; the appeal does not suspend the rejection, and a parallel fresh reservation may be filed. Once granted, the reservation is valid for 30 calendar days and may be extended once for a further 30 days where imminent incorporation can be demonstrated by a notary appointment or executed bank-capital block.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Restricted and non-exclusive. Article 100-2 of the Law of 10 August 1915, as reformed by the Law of 10 August 2016, requires the SARL to maintain a real operational registered office in Luxembourg. A bare mailbox-only 'virtual office' with no personnel, local management presence or accessible records may formally satisfy the RCS address requirement but will not satisfy Luxembourg tax substance doctrine (circular LIR No. 56bis and the anti-abuse rules in the Law of 27 December 2019). For this low-risk EdTech subscription business, a serviced office or dedicated co-working suite with a Luxembourg-resident manager or outsourced local administrative presence is sufficient and recommended.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low - approximately 10% annual probability for a clean, low-risk EdTech SARL in the RCS framework. Unannounced physical inspections are exceptional and occur mainly through tax-audit visits, AML/CFT supervisory checks under CSSF mandates, or RBE substance verification. With a genuine office address, timely filings and a local manager, the probability drops to below 5%.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company name clearance and reservation fee (depot de nom au RCS)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff fixed by the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 19 December 2002, as amended; EUR 40 per standard electronic name reservation

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (notably by the Law of 23 September 2020 modernizing the SARL); SARL regime under Articles 710-1 to 710-23, particularly Articles 710-3 (minimum capital), 710-8 (subscription and payment of shares), and 710-11 (management), together with the Law of 19 December 2002 on the Trade and Companies Register and Company Accounting.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, 'RCS'), administered under the District Court of Luxembourg through the Luxembourg Business Registers ('LBR') electronic e-filing platform.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Deed of Incorporation (Acte constitutif) comprising the coordinated Articles of Association (Statuts coordonnés), filed via RCS electronic Form F1, followed by mandatory publication in the official electronic journal (Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations, 'RESA').
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: EUR 12,000 minimum subscribed capital, fully paid in cash and deposited into a blocked escrow account (compte bloqué) with a Luxembourg credit institution before incorporation; in-kind contributions require a statutory auditor's certificate from a réviseur d'entreprises; the blocked funds are released only after RCS registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: At a constitutive meeting held in Luxembourg City on [date], the founding shareholders resolved: (1) the share capital of EUR 12,000, divided into 1,000 shares of EUR 12, is fully subscribed and paid; (2) the Articles are adopted and the registered office is fixed in the Commune of Luxembourg; (3) [Name] is appointed as Manager (Gérant), with sole authority to open bank accounts, execute the lease, and hire staff; (4) the Manager is authorised to complete the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register filing and the RESA publication; and (5) the EdTech language-learning business under ISIC 6201 and the Apple IAP/Google Play subscription model are approved.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Notarization of the Articles of Incorporation with Blocked Capital Deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg civil-law notary (Chambre des Notaires) and a chosen Luxembourg credit institution (CSSF-regulated)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a Luxembourg notary to draft the Statuts and coordinate the incorporation file. Reserve the proposed corporate name via the RCS e-portal. Open a temporary blocked account with a Luxembourg bank and deposit the full EUR 12,000 minimum capital, obtaining a bank certificate of irrevocable deposit. Sign the notarial deed of incorporation before the notary, who verifies the legal capacity of shareholders, the legality of the business purpose, and the proof of capital payment. The notary then transmits the deed and registration file electronically to the RCS.
required_dossiers: RCS corporate name reservation certificate
Draft Articles of Association (Statuts)
Bank certificate evidencing the deposit of EUR 12,000 in the blocked account
Valid passport or national identity card of each founding shareholder and the appointed manager
Certified proof of registered office address (lease or ownership title)
Business description covering ISIC 6201 EdTech language-learning software
Anti-money-laundering declarations and beneficial ownership particulars
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or bank issues a query, correct the identified deficiencies (e.g., amend the corporate purpose wording or provide updated certified identity documents) and re-sign the deed; if the requested name is refused by the RCS, reserve an alternative name and proceed without losing the capital deposit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Registration with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RCS e-filing service operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) under the District Court of Luxembourg
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary submits the full incorporation dossier through the authorized RCS e-filing channel using Form F1. The RCS verifies the statutory compliance of the deed, the lawfulness of the corporate purpose, and the correctness of the manager appointments. Upon approval, the RCS assigns the definitive RCS registration number, legal form code, and issues the certificate of registration; the company acquires legal personality as of the registration date.
required_dossiers: Notarized deed of incorporation
Coordinated Articles of Association
Certificate of capital deposit issued by the Luxembourg bank
Form F1 completed and signed by the notary
Copy of the manager's consent to appointment
Proof of registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query, the notary submits revised or supplementary documents within 15 calendar days; if the filing is rejected, correct the formal defects and resubmit; any delay is cured without re-depositing capital, provided the blocked account remains valid.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Mandatory Publication in the Official Electronic Journal (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA), published under the Luxembourg Ministry of Justice via LBR
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon RCS registration, the registry automatically generates the legal notice and transmits it for publication in RESA. The notary and the manager verify within three business days that the publication contains all mandatory particulars: corporate name, legal form, registered office, capital, managers, and RCS number. The publication date is the reference point for the opposability of the company's existence and statutory provisions to third parties.
required_dossiers: RCS registration number and certificate
RCS excerpt (extrait) confirming the registration particulars
Notary's filing confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If RESA publication is delayed or contains errors, request an immediate rectification from LBR; the registry must republish the corrected notice; failure to obtain timely publication does not affect the company's existence vis-à-vis the RCS, but third-party opposability commences only upon complete and correct publication.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Registrations: Business Establishment Permit, VAT, and Social Security
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministère de l'Économie via the Guichet.lu portal; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Where the appointed Manager exercises an active management mandate, file the application for the establishment permit (autorisation d'établissement) on Guichet.lu together with the required professional qualification evidence. Register the company for VAT with the AEDT using Form 101, declaring the EdTech subscription services and expected intra-community and B2C supplies. If the company will hire employees, register as an employer with the CCSS; obtain the business registration number applicable to all commercial documents and invoices.
required_dossiers: Notarized deed of incorporation and RCS excerpt
Valid identity document and Luxembourg criminal record certificate of the Manager
Certificate of professional qualification or management experience for the establishment permit
VAT registration form (Formulaire 101)
Employer registration declaration to CCSS
Description of the subscription-based language-learning platform and payment rails (Apple IAP, Google Play Billing)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Ministry of Economy queries the establishment permit application, submit the requested documentation within one month; a refusal may be appealed to the Minister and subsequently to the administrative courts. VAT registration is automatic, but the AEDT may request clarification of the place of supply; respond promptly to avoid default assessments. CCSS registrations are processed within days and may be corrected upon written request.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of the Operating Bank Account and Release of Blocked Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the RCS excerpt, the notarized deed, and the beneficial ownership declarations to the selected commercial bank. Complete the corporate KYC and AML documentation, identifying all shareholders benefiting from more than 25% of the capital. Upon completion of the account opening, instruct the bank to release the EUR 12,000 blocked capital into the operational current account. Execute merchant agreements enabling the Apple IAP and Google Play Billing subscription rails and the registration of the corporate bank account for subsequent treasury and tax operations.
required_dossiers: RCS excerpt (extrait) dated within three months
Certified copy of the Articles of Association
Identity documents of the Manager and all beneficial owners
Beneficial ownership declaration in accordance with the Law of 13 January 2019
Corporate KYC forms and source-of-wealth evidence for shareholders
Business narrative and platform description for payment gateway underwriting
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank defers the account opening or KYC validation, provide supplementary source-of-funds and business documentation without delay; if the application is declined, approach alternative banks preserving the blocked capital; the blocked deposit remains protected pending re-attribution to an operating account.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable; no sector-specific industrial licensing board mandates apply to pure software and interactive language-learning services. The general business establishment permit is governed by the Ministère de l'Économie (Direction générale de l'industrie), while the trade registry and employment oversight rest with the RCS and the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No sectoral operating or manufacturing permit required; only the general establishment permit (autorisation d'établissement) for the Manager and standard RCS/company-law registrations are applicable to the EdTech subscription activity.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Luxembourg Environment Agency), under the Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Sustainable Development
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category D - EIA Exempt: the activity consists exclusively of software development and cloud-based language tutoring with no physical production facility, no land-use change, and no stationary emission sources.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No wastewater, VOC, or industrial waste streams are generated; applicable compliance thresholds are limited to office waste handling under Luxembourg municipal waste regulations, data-center indirect energy consumption, and the general duty of care in the Law of 21 March 2012 on waste management.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The registered office requires a municipal fire-safety conformity statement under the Grand-Ducal Regulation on fire protection; structural load clearance is limited to standard office-use certification in the building safety file. Workplace clearance and occupational health compliance are audited by the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) under the Luxembourg Labor Code, including electrical installation checks and ergonomic workstation assessments; no heavy industrial civil-defense permits apply.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT; unified filing via MyGuichet.lu portal and electronic filing services (eCDF).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a newly incorporated LU SARL, the notary files the incorporation deed with the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), which triggers issuance of a national business identification number (matricule). The entity must file a registration form with the AEDT to obtain a Luxembourg VAT number once taxable turnover exceeds EUR 35,000 or upon the first taxable transaction. Non-established foreign entities making taxable supplies register directly through MyGuichet.lu; a fiscal representative may be required unless the EU One-Stop-Shop (OSS) applies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (resident company subject to corporate income tax, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax; worldwide income taxable with foreign tax credit relief; no pass-through election for SARL).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: VAT grouping election (assujetti unique) under Art. 60 LTV; fiscal integration (intégration fiscale) under Art. 164bis LIR for corporate income tax and municipal business tax requiring a 98% plus participation; optional EU OSS/non-Union OSS scheme for digital services and distance sales; no check-the-box regime under Luxembourg direct tax law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée – TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover for small-business exemption (Art. 57 LTV), except for certain supply categories; EUR 10,000 annual turnover threshold for pan-EU distance sales and digital B2C services subject to the One-Stop-Shop; no mandatory registration threshold for intra-Community acquisitions other than the EUR 10,000 distance-sales threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No nationwide real-time fiscal clearance or pre-clearance API mandate. B2G e-invoicing is mandatory via the PEPPOL network (since 1 March 2019) for invoices to public entities. B2B/B2C e-invoicing is optional; accepted formats include Factur-X, UBL, and CII; digital signatures or EDI controls must be implemented to guarantee authenticity and integrity of invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT applies to dispatches of goods to destinations outside the EU (Art. 52 LTV) and to services directly linked to export transactions. B2B services to non-EU recipients are outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT under the place-of-supply rules (Art. 53 LTV); B2C digital services to non-EU customers likewise fall outside Luxembourg VAT. Zero-rating requires proof of physical export (or direct link for services) and receipt of payment from the non-resident customer.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (with DAE reference number) or electronic export declaration lodged with Luxembourg/other EU customs authority
Bill of Lading / Airway Bill / CMR transport document evidencing physical movement of goods from the EU
Inward Remittance Certificate (bank or foreign-exchange confirmation showing payment received from the non-resident buyer)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg tax authorities may disallow zero-rating if substantiation documents are missing, incomplete, late, or contradictory, triggering reversed VAT assessment at 17% plus default interest of 0.6% per month. Negligent non-compliance may attract fines of 10%–20% of the tax at stake; deliberate fraud or forgery in export substantiation exposes the taxpayer to penalties up to 100% of the evaded VAT and criminal prosecution under Art. 65–69 of the Luxembourg VAT Law.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), operating within the Eurosystem under the European Central Bank (ECB) for monetary policy, FX operations, and TARGET2 settlement. Prudential and AML/CFT supervision of credit institutions and financial-sector entities is exercised by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF), applying the Law of 5 April 1993 on the financial sector, CSSF Regulation 12-02, and CSSF Circulars 20/744 and 22/810.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro (EUR) is fully convertible on both current and capital accounts. Luxembourg has no exchange-control legislation restricting inbound capital injection, outbound trade disbursements, dividend distribution, interest payments, or liquidation proceeds. Free movement of capital is constitutionally embedded via Articles 63-66 TFEU and the OECD Code of Liberalisation of Capital Movements; no prior licensing, notification, or surrender approval is required for EdTech subscription royalties, Apple IAP / Google Play Billing receivables, or intercompany settlements. Profit-repatriation frictions are limited to tax friction only: (i) 15% Luxembourg withholding tax on dividends (reducible to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive 2011/96/EU for qualifying parent entities, or reduced under bilateral double-tax treaties); (ii) 15% withholding tax on interest on profit-sharing loans (non-applicable to arm's-length ordinary shareholder debt); and (iii) statutorily stronger substance expectations for holding/treasury functions under Luxembourg domestic substance rules (Law of 21 December 2017 and circulars), not as a capital-control measure. No restrictions apply to conversion of USD-subscription proceeds into EUR at market rates; banks apply standard FX spread with no spread cap other than market transparency rules under MIFIR.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg imposes zero export-proceeds surrender obligations, zero mandatory conversion ratios, and no statutory repatriation timeline. Software licensing and EdTech subscription export proceeds (ISIC 6201) may be retained indefinitely in EUR, USD, GBP, or any freely convertible currency. The only administrative obligation is statistical: BCL balance-of-payments (BoP) and international investment position (IIP) reporting is executed by the relevant bank on its own initiative for direct investment and services flows above de-minimis thresholds; the SARL has no client-side filing duty for ordinary subscription collections.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational multi-currency EUR/USD current account; dedicated segregated 'compte séquestre' or blocked deposit account can be structured by agreement to serve capital-escrow / notary-blocking functions

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE / Spuerkeess)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational current account in EUR with sub-account capabilities; escrow-style blocked accounts available under contract; conservative AML posture suited to straight-forward SaaS capital structures
Operational EUR/USD account plus separate fiduciary deposit account for escrow; full transaction-banking suite (SWIFT, SEPA, Target2, trade finance)
Operational multi-currency account; global transaction-banking platform with commercial LC, documentary collections, and FX derivative lines under standard ISDA
Operational current account with digital-first onboarding; FX hedging and derivatives desk available subject to board-approved risk policy

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Medium. Luxembourg-authorised or EU-passported Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) and Payment Institutions (PIs) under PSD2 may lawfully hold the SARL's operational funds, segregate client funds, and route cross-border payouts via SEPA/SWIFT; their viability is acceptable for collection-clearing and disbursement-of-royalty rails only. Legal constraints: (1) EMI funds are not deposits and are protected at a lower tier than credit institutions – the FGDL (Fonds de garantie des dépôts Luxembourg) EUR 100,000-per-depositor guarantee applies only to licensed banks; (2) EMIs cannot issue commercial letters of credit or provide unsecured FX credit lines, making them unsuitable for trade settlement and capital-escrow functions; (3) treasury cash concentration above EUR 100,000 at an EMI would be unprotected and is sub-optimal for a Luxembourg parent treasury; (4) CSSF Circular 20/744 vigilance duties apply equally to EMIs, so no KYC relief is obtained. Recommended structure: use a Tier-1 bank as the primary treasury and capital-escrow provider; use an EMI only for instant-settlement of app-store or affiliate micro-disbursements with daily zero-balancing sweeps to the Tier-1 bank, thereby limiting counterparty risk.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No statutory universal mandate for physical attendance exists under the Law of 12 November 2004 (AML/CFT, as amended) or CSSF Regulation 12-02; however, CSSF supervisory expectations and the institution-specific risk appetite of Tier-1 banks in practice require at least one natural-person director or authorised signatory (preferably the 25%+ UBO) to undergo an identity interview. Domestic incumbents (BIL, BCEE, BNP Paribas Lux, SocGen Lux) generally accept remote opening via secured video-conference with e-identification for EU-resident signatories; non-EU resident directors must submit notarially certified passport copies bearing an apostille (Hague Convention 1961), a recent proof-of-address statement (under 3 months), and a personal CV. Where the SARL is managed by a Luxembourg corporate director (PSC), the corporate director's own RCS extract and its beneficial-owner declaration must be produced. Fully remote opening without any live interview is available only at select digital-first institutions (including ING Luxembourg's digital flow for standard corporates), contingent on all signatories being EU-resident and no PEP flagging. Practical mandate for Stage 4: schedule a physical or video KYC appointment for the CEO plus one board member before account activation; the banking mandate must authorise at least two signatories with dual-signature threshold above EUR 50,000 for treasury controls.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO chain opacity, nominee shareholdings, or a trust/corporate layer above the SARL obscuring the ultimate economic owner
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: RBE (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs) registration certificate for the SARL; full corporate organigram with each intermediate entity's shareholders; passport copies and source-of-wealth statements of all natural-person UBOs; notarized declaration confirming the absence of undisclosed nominees; for any corporate shareholder, its own RBE extract; if a trust is involved, the trust deed, protector consent, and TFRA-registered trust details.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border counterparty exposure of the EdTech platform to sanctions-listed or high-risk jurisdictions via app-store users or partner resellers
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Automated restricted-party screening report (EU Consolidated List, OFAC SDN, UN Security Council) covering all contracting counterparties, affiliates, resellers, and app-store merchant accounts; written geoblocking and export-control policy refusing service to embargoed jurisdictions; classification memorandum confirming the software is EAR 5D002 / EU dual-use exempt and not a controlled export; AML risk-assessed customer-jurisdiction matrix; monthly transaction-monitoring output.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Revenue booked through Apple IAP / Google Play Billing where the app-store operator (Apple Distribution International / Google Ireland Ltd or Google Payment Corp.) acts as Merchant of Record, distorting the SARL's receivables trail
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apple Developer Program Agreement and Google Play Distribution Agreement evidencing Merchant-of-Record mechanics; licence and royalty agreement between the SARL and the app-store merchant entity priced at arm's length; monthly settlement statements and tax invoices reconciled to the general ledger by product line; Luxembourg transfer-pricing file (Law of 28 December 2018 and OECD DEMPE analysis) demonstrating that the SARL owns the IP, performs development functions, and retains residual profit.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-EU parent injecting large intercompany loans or share-premium (agio) above EUR 250,000, triggering enhanced source-of-funds reviews
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed intercompany loan agreement with arm's-length interest rate benchmarked under OECD Chapter VI and documented in the Luxembourg transfer-pricing file; source-of-funds evidence (parent bank statements for the six months preceding the injection); Luxembourg corporate tax residence certificate; board minutes approving the borrowing and its commercial purpose; if treated as equity, the notarized deed of capital increase plus RCS/ACD registration proof; no profit-participating character to avoid the 15% withholding risk.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: (1) Equity share capital or share-premium injection must be routed via SWIFT MT103 from the parent's bank to the SARL account using remittance information 'CAPITAL INCREASE - [SARL name] - [notarial deed date/no.]'; the Luxembourg notary's capital certificate will be issued against bank confirmation of availability; (2) Subordinated shareholder loans must be transferred with reference 'INTERCOMPANY LOAN - [loan agreement date]' and the cited loan agreement must be annotated in the bank's field 70 (Remittance Information) to prevent AML misclassification; the loan balance must be disclosed in the annual statutory accounts and reported to the Luxembourg tax administration (ACD) for thin-capitalization and interest-deduction purposes; (3) BCL BoP statistics classify inbound direct-equity flows under EBOPS code 611 and intercompany debt under 612; the bank files these automatically, but the SARL must provide the corporate-event documentation (notarial deed, RCS filing confirmation) for the bank's file; (4) For USD-denominated injections, conversion to EUR occurs at the bank's spot rate on value date; no prior BCL approval is required; (5) Funds must reach the bank account by day 8 before the notarisation date for cash contributions; standard SEPA CT execution is T+0/T+1 and SWIFT MT103 is T+2, so wire initiation must be set no later than T-3 business days.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Multi-rail matrix: (1) EUR payments to EU counterparties settle via SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) with IBAN-only routing, T+0/T+1, zero FX cost; (2) non-EUR or non-SEPA payments use SWIFT MT103 with full remittance data; the bank applies OFAC/EU-list screening and completes ODD on each beneficiary; typical USD clearing via BNP Paribas New York or SocGen New York branches, T+2; (3) large-value EUR disbursements above EUR 1 million must be routed via Target2 through the bank's central-bank account for real-time finality, avoiding bilateral credit risk; (4) trade settlements with content-suppliers and localization partners may be effected via Documentary Collection (D/P) or Commercial Letters of Credit (L/C) under UCP 600; the SARL's Luxembourg bank issues the L/C for confirmed supplier commitments, with payment against presented shipping/invoice documents; (5) recurring affiliate and publisher royalties are paid through bulk SEPA B2B Direct Debit for EU partners or SWIFT FileAct MT1xx/MT9xx batch files for non-EU partners; (6) Apple IAP / Google Play Billing commissions (typically 15% to 30%) are settled by Apple/Google as Merchant of Record and are outside the SARL's direct outbound rail, but the SARL receives monthly settlement statements that reconcile to its revenue ledger; any dispute-chargebacks or refunds are netted by the platform before settlement; (7) all outbound disbursements above EUR 50,000 require dual electronic signature authorisation under the banking mandate; batch payments are executed only on Tuesdays and Thursdays to centralise liquidity.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright EUR/USD FX Forward (plain vanilla) with maturity up to 24 months, booked under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or short-form FX Master Agreement; board-approved hedging policy limits cover up to 75% of forecast net USD subscription inflows rolling 12 months
FX Swap (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP) for rolling subscription-receivable conversion and liquidity management
Cross-Currency Interest Rate Swap (CCS) to hedge USD- or GBP-denominated intercompany loan principal and interest against EUR functional-currency volatility

Non-Deliverable Forward (NDF) on exotics such as INR (India app-store settlements) or BRL where local deliverability constraints exist; permitted only with BCL/CSSF-licensed banks under approved credit lines; not applicable to EUR which is fully deliverable

European-style FX options (EUR call / USD put and EUR put / USD call) purchased with zero upfront structures (cost-bearing) at Tier-1 banks, subject to the SARL's derivatives capacity assessment under EMIR and the board's no-speculation policy
Collateralised Rolling Spot with Credit Support Annex (CSA) under ISDA, enabling same-day USD/EUR conversion without accruing open-forward exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Hold ordinary annual general meeting to approve annual accounts, act on profit allocation, and discharge directors/managers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders; minutes recorded and retained in the statutory minute book at the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of financial year end; calendar-year SARL must hold the AGM by 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No direct administrative fine, but failure prevents lawful approval and filing of annual accounts; directors/managers may be held jointly liable and may be compelled by court order to convene the meeting

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: File statutory annual accounts (balance sheet, profit and loss account, notes, and auditor's report where applicable) in the prescribed RCS format
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), electronic filing via eJustice/eCDF
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months of financial year end; calendar-year SARL must file by 31 July of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may trigger a formal notice, court-ordered filing, and an administrative fine against directors/managers of up to EUR 5,000; persistent non-filing may result in administrative strike-off or dissolution proceedings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial ownership in the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) operated by Luxembourg Business Registers / RCS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 1 month of the anniversary of the initial RBE registration; any updating event must be filed within 1 month of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-confirmation or late update is a criminal offence; responsible directors/managers may be subject to fines up to EUR 1,250,000 and imprisonment under Luxembourg AML law, in addition to administrative sanctions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual internal audit and verification of the statutory corporate registers (members, directors/managers, share transfers) and RCS/UBO information consistency
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate governance file retained at registered office; RCS registers updated where discrepancies are identified
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: To be completed immediately after the AGM and no later than the annual accounts filing deadline (31 July for calendar-year SARL)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Incorrect or omitted register entries are unenforceable against third parties; managers may be personally liable for damages arising from erroneous or incomplete statutory registers

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Statutory audit is required where the SARL exceeds two of the three small-company thresholds: balance sheet total EUR 4.4 million, net turnover EUR 8.8 million, and average headcount 50. Audit is also mandatory for parent undertakings required to prepare consolidated accounts exceeding the group thresholds (balance sheet total EUR 17.5 million, net turnover EUR 35 million, average 250 employees), unless a specific consolidation exemption applies.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the Law of 19 December 2002 on the commercial register and accounting obligations, as amended; IFRS is mandatory for consolidated accounts of issuers admitted to trading on an EU regulated market.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SARL must confirm annually, within one month of the anniversary of the initial RBE registration, that beneficial owner information remains accurate. Any transfer of shares resulting in a 25% or greater ownership/voting change requires a renewed RBE filing within one month of the transfer. The register of members must be updated continuously and independently verified against each transfer instrument.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,500 - USD 16,000 per year when audit is mandatory

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% (combined CIT 17% + solidarity surcharge of 7% on CIT + municipal business tax at Luxembourg City rate 6.75%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: IP Box regime: 80% exemption on qualifying IP-derived income, yielding an effective combined rate of approximately 5.0%. Additional 8% investment tax credit for eligible digital and tangible fixed assets.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 540 (Corporate Income Tax Return) filed electronically via eCDF (Electronic Corporate Tax Declaration) on the MyGuichet.lu portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (fiscal year normally aligned to calendar year; separate filings for CIT, MBT, and NWT are consolidated in Form 540)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 31 March of the year following the tax year; extended automatically to 31 December when filed electronically via eCDF.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income before loss carryforward and special deductions (comprising worldwide profit, adjusted per Luxembourg GAAP and tax law).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report non-resident allocable income only if the SARL has a Luxembourg permanent establishment or source taxable income; otherwise enter zero.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses brought forward from prior years (unlimited carryforward, but subject to anti-abuse rules on change of ownership).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident shareholders with direct tax exposure, losses of the SARL are not available; file on the entity's behalf only.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: IP Box deduction – 80% exemption on net qualifying IP income (per Luxembourg IP regime). Attach detailed schedule and supporting records.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident owner must ensure arm's-length royalty agreements with the SARL are in place; any sub-licensed IP must be documented.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credits (unilateral or treaty relief) for cross-border income already taxed abroad.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide Form 2 (foreign tax credit claim) and foreign tax assessment certificate; allocate credits only to the SARL's profits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax base after deductions (Box 1 minus Box 2 and Box 3 adjustments). Subject to CIT at 17%.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders should verify that no income attributable to a foreign PE of the SARL is included; PE carve-outs apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Municipal Business Tax (MBT) base – generally the same taxable income as for CIT, allocated to the local municipality where the SARL is registered.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For SARL with a commercial presence in Luxembourg, MBT applies to the full base; non-resident branch income exempt if permanent establishment abroad.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of 10% of the tax due (minimum €250), plus default interest of 0.6% per month (or fraction thereof). Intentional failure may attract criminal fines up to €250,000 or imprisonment of up to 5 years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% (domestic law); reduced to 0% for qualifying EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive dividends and up to 5% under certain tax treaties (subject to holding period and substance requirements).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a reduced dividend withholding rate, the non-resident beneficial owner must submit a valid tax residency certificate (TRC) from its tax authority to the Luxembourg paying agent before dividend payment. The SARL must file a withholding tax return (Form 280) and attach the TRC. For EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive relief, the parent must hold at least 10% of the SARL's shares continuously for 12 months and provide a declaration of substance and entitlement. Failure to provide TRC results in application of the statutory 15% rate, subject to later refund.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties and interest paid to non-residents: 0% Luxembourg withholding tax under domestic law (since 2020 for royalties and interest, aligning with the EU Interest and Royalties Directive). No treaty rate applies because no source taxation is levied.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 10 million of total revenues for the Luxembourg entity triggers the mandatory Local File. Master File is required when the worldwide group's consolidated revenue exceeds EUR 750 million. Intercompany transactions above EUR 1 million per category (goods, services, intangibles, financing) require contemporaneous TP documentation.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg applies OECD ATAD substance requirements. A SARL must demonstrate adequate physical presence (stand-alone office), qualified local employees, and substantive decision-making in Luxembourg to access tax treaty and EU Directive benefits. Absent such substance, the entity may be considered a shell company, leading to denial of treaty relief, recapture of withholding tax, and potential reclassification of the entity for Luxembourg tax purposes.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission of taxable revenues, falsification of accounting books, claiming ineligible IP box exemptions, or filing a materially inaccurate Form 540.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine up to €250,000 and imprisonment of up to 5 years; civil penalty of 10%–20% of evaded tax plus default interest at 0.6% per month.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign false tax filings are jointly and severally liable for the evaded tax; they may face criminal prosecution and imprisonment. Under the Luxembourg Company Law, the corporate veil is pierced if the director acted in bad faith.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Renting a virtual office with no employees, absence of local board meetings, passive holding of IP without active management, or operating a purely artificial arrangement to claim tax treaty benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of tax treaty benefits and EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive relief; recapture of withholding tax on distributed dividends; imposition of additional CIT/MBT on profits attributable to Luxembourg substance; potential administrative fine of €10,000–€100,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for unpaid corporate tax under veil-piercing doctrine if the shell company is used to evade public obligations; travel bans and asset freezes may be imposed under EU Directive 2014/42/EU.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to prepare or maintain contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation, using non-arm's-length royalty rates for IP, overpaying management fees to foreign affiliates, or entering into round-tripping financing structures.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer pricing adjustment of understated profits; penalty of up to €25,000 for missing documentation; default interest at 0.6% per month; on concealment, a penalty of 200% of the tax understated.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for the adjustment amount if they orchestrated the mispricing without legitimate business purpose; criminal negligence can lead to imprisonment for up to 3 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the EdTech platform via Apple/Google IAP without adequate anti-money-laundering controls (KYC thresholds not met for merchants), or concealing the beneficial owner of the SARL despite substantial digital payment volumes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines from €10,000 to €250,000, or up to 5% of annual turnover for serious breaches; criminal sanctions for institutional offenses under Luxembourg AML law; business license revocation for payment processor relationships.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be subject to personal fines up to €1,000,000, travel bans, and imprisonment of up to 5 years for gross negligence in failing to prevent money laundering through the entity's payment rails.
